objective: GroupGuard only handles command intake, intranet requests, protocol validation, and OneBot delivery. Public upstream access, business processing, rendering, caching, and degradation are owned by lolapisevers.

steps.summary: Create one intranet query client shared by real commands and admin tests.
Remove plugin-side shard data download, hero matching, sorting, rendering decisions, and public fallback.
Move battle, ARAM, and ban commands to the final delivery envelope.
Keep one intranet API base for built-in LoL queries and deprecate public upstream configuration.
Add an architecture test that rejects public upstream access from built-in query modules.
Deploy GroupGuard after the compatible service release and perform real-member acceptance tests.

current_findings.summary: The shard command directly downloads public shard and hero JSON from the SnowLuma container.
Built-in ban query still supports direct public primary and backup providers even though production uses the intranet service.
The plugin still interprets and formats business data instead of consuming a final delivery payload.

next_recommended_action.summary: Implement an atomic persistent snapshot store before changing GroupGuard runtime code.

production_rule: Deploy lolapisevers first, verify backward compatibility, then deploy GroupGuard. Never restore plugin-side public fallback.
